usage: This is the standard, everyday way to ask someone where they are from in the Levant. It is used in both casual and formal situations, though in highly formal contexts one might use '7adertak' instead of 'enta'. The word order can also be flipped to 'enta min ween?' without changing the meaning.

variants.label: to a man
variants.note: The standard form used when addressing a single male.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: The standard form used when addressing a single female.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Used when addressing two or more people.

variants.label: formal (to a man)
variants.note: Used to show respect to older men or in professional settings.

variants.label: formal (to a woman)
variants.note: Used to show respect to older women or in professional settings.

examples.arabic: أَهلاً، فُرسَة سَعِيدَة. مِن وِين إِنتَ؟
examples.transliteration: ahlan, forsa sa3iida. min ween enta?
examples.english: Hello, nice to meet you. Where are you from?
Excuse me, where are you (pl.) from?
